target_customer: Companies running logistics, scheduling, routing and packing optimization, such as airlines and shippers
problem: Combinatorial optimization jobs (scheduling pilots, packing containers) run slowly and expensively on general purpose cloud hardware; the company proposes processors shaped to the memory access patterns of Karp's 21 NP-complete problems.
business_model: Cloud deployed optimization hardware, sold as scalable capacity without hardware or firmware expertise needed
product_category: Custom processors and hardware for combinatorial optimization

founders.name: David Cox
founders.background_notes: YC page: founded the company December 2021, full time from March 2022. Background not listed. The YC page also names Brycen as a contact but not a founder; a seed data site says it was founded by Brycen Wershing, unverified.

competitors.name: Fujitsu Digital Annealer
competitors.what: Application specific CMOS hardware for fully connected QUBO optimization, offered as a cloud service
competitors.traction_then: Second generation cloud service for logistics and finance available to customers

competitors.name: Toshiba Simulated Bifurcation Machine (SQBM+)
competitors.what: FPGA based Ising machine for large scale combinatorial optimization
competitors.traction_then: Joined Microsoft Azure Quantum network in 2020-09 and scaled out in 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing custom processor microarchitecture is research grade work for a one person team; the performance claims (7,000x on subset sum) are company statements not independently verified.

defensibility.rationale: A novel microarchitecture could be hard to copy if it works, but it is unproven, and Fujitsu and Toshiba already sell optimization hardware.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found; the company remained a tiny team.

market_need_then: Logistics optimization is expensive on cloud solvers (the launch post cites Google OR-Tools cost) and TechCrunch's batch coverage said there is clearly a customer base, though the claim is ambitious.

branding.domain_note: Uses integrated-reasoning.com; a search result also mentions ir.design, unverified.

identity.mascot_or_character: Honu microarchitecture name (Hawaiian for sea turtle), name origin not sourced

branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch listed it among the biggest moonshots of the S22 batch (2022-09).

brand_strength.rationale: Generic descriptive name with limited coverage beyond a batch roundup.

outcome_analysis: Integrated Reasoning is active with a one person team and was called a moonshot by TechCrunch in its Summer 2022 batch coverage. Aggregators report roughly $0.5M pre-seed and $1.9M total, not confirmed by a primary source. No customers, benchmarks by third parties or funding announcements were found, so its progress against Fujitsu and Toshiba optimization hardware cannot be judged.
notes: VCBacked reports $1.9M seed total with last round announced June 2025 and investors Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, 1984 Ventures, Pegasus Tech Ventures and Four Cities Capital; another source says $500K pre-seed. Aggregators only, so no round recorded. Location differs between sources (San Diego on the YC page, San Francisco elsewhere). Fujitsu source is undated, so source_date is null. The Honu meaning is my label of an unsourced name and should be treated as unknown.
